title: 3rd Truth Ease Amid Speed And Multiplicity And The Gradelessness Of Power

questions.question: What main subject is explained in this passage?
questions.answer: It explains how Allah creates living things very quickly, in huge numbers, and with perfect order and skill.

questions.question: Which kinds of created things are especially pointed out in the passage?
questions.answer: Plants and animals are especially mentioned.

questions.question: What surprising combination is repeated in the description of creation?
questions.answer: The passage says creation happens with speed and ease while still showing great care, beauty, and order.

questions.question: How does the passage describe the worth of created things even though they are found in large numbers?
questions.answer: It says they still have value and special qualities even when they are many and mixed together.

questions.question: According to the passage, who alone can create in this way?
questions.answer: Only the One Allah, whose power has no difficulty with anything.

questions.question: What does the passage teach about the relationship between large things and small things for Divine power?
questions.answer: It teaches that both are equally easy for Allah to create.

questions.question: What comparison is made between stars and atoms?
questions.answer: Creating stars is just as easy for Allah as creating atoms.

questions.question: What comparison is made between a whole kind of creature and one individual from it?
questions.answer: Allah creates an entire species as easily as one member of that species.

questions.question: What examples are given to show that bringing life is easy for Allah?
questions.answer: Giving life to the whole earth is described as just as easy as giving life to a tree.

questions.question: What example shows that huge size does not make creation harder for Allah?
questions.answer: A very large tree and a tiny seed are both equally easy for Him to create.

questions.question: What is the main conclusion a student should take from this passage?
questions.answer: Allah’s power is unlimited, so creating many things, great things, and small things is all equally easy for Him.

questions.question: How are speed and order connected in the passage?
questions.answer: The passage shows that living things are made very fast without losing order.

questions.question: How are ease and skill connected in the passage?
questions.answer: It says Allah creates with complete ease while also showing perfect skill and ability.

questions.question: Why is abundance not a problem in the passage’s argument?
questions.answer: Because even when creatures are many and mixed together, they are still made without confusion or defect.

questions.question: What does the passage say about confusion and deficiency in creation?
questions.answer: It says true creation happens without either of them.

questions.question: What kind of power is described as able to do this?
questions.answer: A unique power for which nothing is difficult.

questions.question: What lesson is taught by the comparison between the greatest thing and the smallest thing?
questions.answer: Size does not limit Allah in any way.

questions.question: What does the passage suggest about creating a universal thing and a small particular thing?
questions.answer: Both are equally easy for Allah.

questions.question: Why does the passage mention the earth, a tree, and a seed together?
questions.answer: To show different levels of size and scope, all of which are equally easy for Allah to create and give life to.

questions.question: What belief about Allah is strengthened by these examples?
questions.answer: Belief in His complete power and uniqueness is strengthened.

questions.question: Write the central message of the passage in one sentence.
questions.answer: Allah alone creates all living things with perfect order, great beauty, and complete ease, no matter how many or how large they are.

questions.question: What is one major sign of Divine power mentioned at the start of the passage?
questions.answer: The creation of plants and animals with both speed and perfect order.

questions.question: Besides speed, what other qualities of creation are highlighted?
questions.answer: Ease, skill, order, value, and distinctness are highlighted.

questions.question: How does the passage describe creatures being found together in large numbers?
questions.answer: It says they are mixed together in abundance but still remain distinct and well-made.

questions.question: What can we understand from the claim that there is no confusion in abundant creation?
questions.answer: Each creature is controlled perfectly and given its proper form.

questions.question: What title or description is given to the Creator in this passage?
questions.answer: He is described as a Unique Being whose power faces no difficulty.

questions.question: What comparison shows that distance in size does not matter to Allah?
questions.answer: The passage compares stars with atoms.

questions.question: What comparison shows that number does not matter to Allah?
questions.answer: A whole species and one individual are said to be equally easy for Him.

questions.question: What comparison shows that broad and limited things are the same for Divine power?
questions.answer: A vast universal reality and a small particular one are both equally easy.

questions.question: What comparison is used about life returning to creation?
questions.answer: Reviving the whole earth is compared to bringing life to a tree.

questions.question: What comparison is used about creating something huge and something tiny?
questions.answer: A mountain-like tree and a very small seed are both said to be equally easy.

questions.question: What effect should these visible examples have on a thoughtful reader?
questions.answer: They should lead the reader to recognize Allah’s unmatched power.

questions.question: In this passage, what is special about the way living things are created?
questions.answer: They are created rapidly, in large numbers, and still with perfect precision.

questions.question: How does the passage balance the ideas of abundance and uniqueness?
questions.answer: It says creatures are many, yet each one still has value and its own distinct form.

questions.question: What does “absolute orderliness” teach us about creation?
questions.answer: It teaches that creation is fully controlled and arranged, not messy or accidental.

questions.question: Why is “extreme ease” important in the passage?
questions.answer: It shows that Allah does not struggle to create, no matter how much He creates.

questions.question: What does “extreme skill” add to the meaning of the passage?
questions.answer: It shows that creation is not only easy for Allah, but also full of wisdom and artistry.

questions.question: What kind of being could make countless creatures without defects?
questions.answer: Only a Being with unlimited power.

questions.question: What does the comparison between stars and atoms teach about limits?
questions.answer: It teaches that Allah’s power is not limited by size.

questions.question: What does the comparison between a species and one member teach about number?
questions.answer: It teaches that Allah’s power is not limited by quantity.

questions.question: What does the comparison between the earth and a tree teach about scale?
questions.answer: It teaches that the size of the task makes no difference to Allah.

questions.question: What does the comparison between a huge tree and a tiny seed teach about complexity?
questions.answer: It teaches that both complex and small things are equally easy for Allah to create.

questions.question: What area of creation does the passage focus on most directly?
questions.answer: It focuses on the coming into being of plants and animals.

questions.question: What does the passage say about the speed of creation?
questions.answer: It says creation happens with complete swiftness.

questions.question: What does the passage say about the quality of creation?
questions.answer: It says creation is orderly, skillful, valuable, and distinct.

questions.question: How does the passage describe creation when things are very numerous?
questions.answer: It says many things are created together without disorder or weakness.

questions.question: What conclusion does the passage draw from that fact?
questions.answer: Such creation can come only from Allah, the One with limitless power.

questions.question: Which examples compare very large and very small created things?
questions.answer: Stars and atoms, a giant tree and a tiny seed.

questions.question: Which examples compare many and one?
questions.answer: A whole species and a single member.

questions.question: Which examples compare a broad living world and one part of it?
questions.answer: The whole earth being revived and a single tree being revived.

questions.question: What does the repeated phrase of equal ease show about Allah’s power?
questions.answer: It shows that His power does not become weaker with bigger or greater tasks.

questions.question: Why are ordinary visible things used as examples in the passage?
questions.answer: Because they help people understand Divine power through things they can notice around them.

questions.question: Give a short summary of the passage.
questions.answer: The passage teaches that Allah creates all living things with perfect order, beauty, and ease, and that the largest and smallest creations are equally easy for Him.

questions.question: What is the “third truth” mainly trying to prove?
questions.answer: It is trying to prove that Allah’s power is unlimited and unique.

questions.question: What kinds of qualities in creation are listed together near the beginning?
questions.answer: Fast creation, perfect order, ease, skill, value, and clear distinction.

questions.question: Why is it important that creatures are distinct even when they are mixed together?
questions.answer: It shows careful control and wisdom in creation.

questions.question: What does the passage say about defects in Allah’s creation?
questions.answer: It says creation happens without defects or confusion.

questions.question: According to the passage, what makes this kind of creation possible?
questions.answer: It is possible because Allah’s power has no difficulty at all.

questions.question: How does the passage compare the creation of the very large and the very small?
questions.answer: It says both are equally easy for Allah.

questions.question: How does the passage compare creating one thing and creating many things?
questions.answer: It says making many is no harder for Allah than making one.

questions.question: What example in the passage deals with bringing dead things back to life?
questions.answer: Giving life again to the whole earth is compared with giving life to a tree.

questions.question: What example in the passage deals with size in plant life?
questions.answer: A very large tree and a seed smaller than a fingertip are compared.

questions.question: What is the purpose of saying these actions happen in front of our eyes?
questions.answer: The purpose is to remind us that the evidence is visible in the world around us.

questions.question: What wrong idea about creation is challenged by this passage?
questions.answer: It challenges the idea that great numbers, large size, or complexity could be too hard to create.
